openingBell.title: The Opening Bell
openingBell.intro: Wednesday, Mercury's day. Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. Mercury is the messenger: quick mind, clean words, fast hands. Breathe slow so you can move fast.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds squares the mind. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then go build.

mindset.body: Washington made its push last night. Tatum answered with 41 and Boston never let go. Every day somebody makes a run at you: a tired body, a distraction, a doubt. You don't panic, you answer. Last workday before the holiday: finish the piece and ship it before the turkey. Competitive. Unbeatable. Always rising. fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Wednesday, Mercury's day: quick and sharp. Run the three blocks, no rest between.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom's RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time.

Wednesday is Mercury's day (Woden's in the old Germanic calendar, mercredi in French). Hermes-Mercury rules speech, trade, travel and quick thinking: the right day to send the message and close the deal.
The 14th-century German mystic wrote: 'If the only prayer you ever say in your entire life is thank you, it will be enough.' A fitting line the day before Thanksgiving.

The 'thrice-great' Hermes of the Hermetic texts blends the Greek Hermes and the Egyptian Thoth, god of writing. To the Hermeticists, mind came first: 'The All is Mind.' Get the thought clear and the work follows.
